Two high-priority defects identified: (1) XSS/JS-injection risk in createPageJumpInput / createBootstrapPageJumpInput — URL template embedded raw in single-quoted JS string; fix with json_encode(). (2) Example 3 feedback display bug — $feedback is set inside processSubmittedActions() callback which runs lazily during echo $grid, AFTER the feedback conditional block has already been printed; feedback alert will never appear.

One design concern: processSubmittedActions() is invoked lazily from generateOutput() rather than eagerly at request start; this limits use of action callbacks for redirects, early exits, or page-level state changes.

One ambiguity: getSelectValue() silently returns '' when no valueColumn is configured while actions are active; checkboxes are rendered but submit empty values with no warning. Acceptable for now but worth a developer note.
All acceptance criteria for WP-007 are met. Defects are in earlier WP code (not the WP-007 housekeeping scope); they are surfaced here for tracking.

comments.note: XSS / JS-injection in createPageJumpInput() (BaseGridRenderer.php line ~500) and createBootstrapPageJumpInput() (Bootstrap5Renderer.php line ~181): the URL template is embedded raw inside a single-quoted JavaScript string literal — e.g., `window.location.href = '{$urlTemplate}'.replace(...)`. A URL containing a single quote breaks the JS, and attacker-controlled query parameters could inject arbitrary JS. Fix: replace `'{$urlTemplate}'` with `json_encode($urlTemplate)` (which produces a double-quoted, properly escaped JS string). Affects both renderer files.

examples/3-grid-actions.php feedback display race condition: the $feedback conditional block (`<?php if ($feedback !== null):?>`) is printed BEFORE `<?= $grid ?>`. The action callback that sets $feedback is only invoked from processSubmittedActions(), which is called lazily inside generateOutput() when the grid is echo'd. By the time the callback runs, the feedback block is already in the output buffer and cannot be updated. The feedback alert will never display. Fix: call `$grid->actions()->processSubmittedActions()` explicitly before starting HTML output (after grid configuration), and remove the implicit-call comment that is misleading.

processSubmittedActions() is invoked lazily from generateOutput() during HTML rendering. This prevents callbacks from performing request-lifecycle operations (redirect, session writes, early exit) before any HTML is flushed. Recommend adding an explicit DataGrid::processActions() method (or calling processSubmittedActions() at the start of a DataGrid::process() step) so callers can control when action side-effects occur, distinct from rendering.

getSelectValue() in StandardRow.php returns '' silently when getValueColumn() is null and actions are active. Checkboxes are rendered but submit empty-string values. A developer using setValueColumn() but then accidentally unsetting it (->setValueColumn(null)) will get silent data loss. Consider logging a warning or throwing in getSelectionCell() if isSelectable() is true but getValueColumn() returns null.

AC2 wording ('exits with 0 errors') conflicts with the actual PHPStan exit code of 1 (14 pre-existing errors). The intent is satisfied (no new errors). For future plans, rephrase ACs to 'introduces no new PHPStan errors' to avoid ambiguity — already flagged by QA, confirmed here.

GridPagination.getPageURLTemplate() uses magic sentinel value 999999999. If the URL contains that numeric substring elsewhere (e.g., an ID that happens to be 999999999), the placeholder substitution will corrupt the URL. This is an existing document constraint. A less collision-prone approach would be a random or UUID-based sentinel, or a hashed placeholder that could not plausibly appear in a real URL.
